title: The driver runs the suite, and a red one goes round once

statements.says: The driver runs the suite as a step of its own and holds the result.
The loop runs eight steps: build, standards, spec, architecture, fix, sweep, suite, finish.
The suite step proves the tests can run, runs them, and keeps the output.
finish no longer runs tests: it commits and closes, and is handed the passing output for the Closing note.
A red suite sends the loop back to fix once, with the failure text in the prompt.
The way back runs fix, then sweep, then suite, never fix straight to suite.
If the suite is still red after that one circuit, the loop stops and leaves the worktree.
Before it runs anything, the suite step checks its preconditions: Docker up, uv present, node_modules in place.
A failing precondition stops the loop and is never handed to a Session.
A red suite is run a second time before it is believed.
land_ticket.py still runs the suite after a rebase.
The driver and land_ticket.py share one way of running the suite.
A test reads STEPS and holds the two documents that list the steps to it.
A prompt carrying a failing suite is fixed under the same --fix flag as review findings.
The suite was the one gate resting on a session's word, so a Session could fix a red suite, commit, and pass every check while carrying comments no sweep saw.
The way back goes through sweep because fix writes and a sweep has to follow the last writer.
A failed test, a suite that would not build, a suite that could not start and a flake all arrive as the same non-zero status, and only two of the four are the ticket's fault.
A failing precondition is never handed to a Session because no Session can start Docker.
A red suite is run again because the container-backed Span tests flake, and a Session handed a failure it cannot reproduce may weaken a test or edit code that was never broken.
land_ticket.py runs the suite to prove the work survived a base that moved.
Sharing one way of running the suite means the preconditions and the command list cannot disagree.
A document that can silently contradict the script is the same defect one layer out.
The retry keeps --fix because it is the same act on a different input.
The second run moved out of the driver because the flake is a fact about this repo, and the driver is Machinery every repo runs.
Having finish stop on a red suite and never fix was rejected, because the loop should fix what it has the information to fix rather than spend a developer to save a driver.
Having finish fix the red suite and sweep its own change before committing was rejected, because a step written into a skill can be skipped and a step in the script cannot.

Having finish keep running the suite and report that it went red was rejected, because the driver would learn the gate's answer from the Session it is checking and the failure text would have to survive a Session that has ended.
Telling the four kinds of failure apart by reading the runner's output was rejected, because it means parsing text that changes with every version of dotnet test and pytest.
Treating the first red as red was rejected, because a flake would then spend the single circuit and hand a Session a failure that is not there.

Two circuits rather than one were rejected, because a Session with the whole ticket and the failure text has already tried, a third attempt is unlikely to differ, and an unattended run wants a small bound.
It replaces the step list in the earlier record on review axes editing and the sweep following the last writer, and nothing else in it.
A later record moved the second run of a red suite out of the driver: the Suite file now sets how many times a red Suite runs, one by default, and this repo's Suite file asks for two.
